title: Al-Fil: the elephant
hook: the army of the elephant and the birds with stones (Surah 105)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Quraysh, the Prophet's tribe, fed against hunger and made safe from fear. Your line was fed and safe. Day one hundred sixty-nine.

A desert town with no walls and no army. Coming up the road from the south is a real army, and with it an elephant, maybe more than one, marching toward the one building the town is known for. The townspeople do the only thing they can. They leave, and they go up into the hills to watch. This happened, according to Muslim tradition, in the year the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born.
screen: `A TOWN WITH NO WALLS.` → `AN ARMY WITH AN ELEPHANT.` → `THEY WATCH FROM THE HILLS.`

segments.voice: Surah one hundred five opens, in Pickthall's translation: Hast thou not seen how thy Lord dealt with the owners of the Elephant? The Qur'an tells it in five lines and names no one. The historians and commentators fill in the names. The army came from Yemen, led by a ruler named Abraha who, the story goes, had built a great church and wanted the Arabs to make pilgrimage there instead of to the Ka'bah. So he marched to destroy it. The early biography of the Prophet keeps a famous scene. Abraha's men seized camels belonging to Abd al-Muttalib, the Prophet's grandfather and a leader of Mecca. He went to Abraha and asked for his camels back. Abraha was surprised: I've come to destroy your holy House, and you ask about camels? And Abd al-Muttalib is remembered as saying: I am the lord of the camels. The House has its own Lord, who will protect it. Then the surah tells what happened. The plan came to nothing. Allah sent birds in flocks, ababil, pelting the army with stones of baked clay, and left them like chewed-up straw. Tradition says the Arabs counted years from it, the Year of the Elephant, and places the Prophet's birth in that year, around five hundred seventy. So the surah reminds Quraysh of something their own elders saw. They didn't defend the House. They couldn't. They went up into the hills. The house was defended.
screen: `THE OWNERS OF THE ELEPHANT.` · `I AM THE LORD OF THE CAMELS.` · `BIRDS IN FLOCKS, STONES OF CLAY.` · `THE YEAR OF THE ELEPHANT.` · then, large: `THE HOUSE WAS DEFENDED.`

segments.voice: Remember a time you were protected, when something could have gone badly and didn't: a near miss on the road, a diagnosis that came back clear, someone who stepped in for you. Notice how little of it you controlled, and let yourself feel the relief again. If you pray, you can say alhamdulillah for it, as if it happened today.
Al-Fil. The elephant, the name of Surah one hundred five, about the army that marched on the Ka'bah. Today's word.
Your line: the house was defended. Abd al-Muttalib asked only for his camels. Day one hundred sixty-nine, done.

howItsDone: Surah al-Fil is recited in the prayers, and the story of Abraha and the Year of the Elephant is taught as part of the Prophet's biography, since tradition places his birth in that year.

fork.reveal: he asked for his camels, and said: I am the lord of the camels; the House has its own Lord, who will protect it.

original.note: Arabic: the elephant; the name of Surah 105.

trapdoor: what you thought: a strange story about birds and an elephant.
what it means: a reminder to Quraysh that the House was protected when they could not protect it.
what a scholar hears: Abraha al-Ashram of Yemen; ababil and sijjil (baked clay) in 105:3–4; the Year of the Elephant is traditionally around 570, though historians debate the date.
recall: the four-line surah about who God is

sources.quoted: Hast thou not seen how thy Lord dealt with the owners of the Elephant?

sources.ref: Qur'an 105:2–5 (the plan undone, the birds, the stones, the chewed straw)

notes: Please confirm the exact Pickthall wording of 105:1.
The camels scene and Abd al-Muttalib's words are from Ibn Ishaq's sirah, paraphrased; the script says 'is remembered as saying'.
Date 'around 570' is traditional; modern historians debate it (some place Abraha's campaign earlier). The trapdoor notes the debate.
'Rarely or never seen' and 'armored' were cut from the hook in review as unsourced.
